entries.text: How the gauge names a distance from the 200-day average, and how it classifies it. It describes where price is, not what it will do; this platform has not measured forward returns for these zones.

is how much the 200-day average itself moved over the last 20 days. The classification calls the average rising only above +0.5%; anything else, including a flat or slowly rising average, counts as not rising.
combines the zone and the slope. It describes where price sits relative to its long-run average; it is not a forecast, and this platform has not measured what followed each classification.
The zones and classifications on this page describe price relative to its 200-day average. They are research tooling, not investment advice, and not a forecast.
Below an average that is not rising
Price is more than 20% above its 200-day simple moving average, a distance it rarely reaches.
